Hi Sean,

Quick ask from our compliance team as we progress to legal review: can you share Redwood's up-to-date subprocessor roster (including vendors that process telemetry, logging, and ephemeral key management) and a short note on any contractors who have temporary elevated access? We need the roster plus evidence files (SOC 2 summary, attestation dates, any per-subprocessor encryption ownership) to include in our SIG review.

We also require a simple statement of where transient logs are stored and retention windows for RKVC/kv-cache logs used in inference debugging. If possible, a CSV mapping subprocessor -> purpose -> region would be ideal.

Thanks — tight timeline for us, so a response by EOD Monday would be appreciated.

— Daniel

Sean / Marissa — draft of the requested statements below. I'm attaching the evidence checklist for Helix.

1) Transient logs used for KV/cache debugging:
- Type: Ephemeral inference routing logs and KV-cache debug artifacts.
- Storage: Encrypted blob store in us-west-2 (S3 with SSE-KMS).
- Retention: Default 7 days for debug artifacts; aggregated telemetry metrics retained 365 days.
- Access: Access restricted to the on-call SRE role and a scoped set of contractors via time-limited IAM sessions; all sessions logged and reviewed weekly.

2) Temporary contractors with elevated access (last 12 months):
- Provider: RuntimeOps (contractor managed pool) — scoped to model kernel optimization tasks; maximum access window 48 hours per incident; privileged sessions require explicit approval and are logged.
- Provider: EdgeLab Consultants — occasional load-testing access, audited per-engagement.

Notes: We include the contractor provider name and a certification that no persistent secrets were provisioned to contractors; ephemeral creds only. If Helix needs per-contractor CVs or SOC attestations, we can request them from the contractor vendors (may add 3–5 business days).

[Attachment: subproc-evidence-checklist.xlsx]

Monica Patel
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
